feature: The bottom row lines up, and double clicking the zoom goes to actual size
summary: Every glass group along the bottom of the canvas is now the same height on one centre line, and double clicking the zoom percentage takes the picture back to a hundred percent while a single click still opens the stop menu.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to switch on. Open any screenshot.

try.do: Look along the bottom of the canvas: tools, colours, grid, zoom.
Zoom in a few times with the slider or a pinch.
Double click the percentage. The picture goes to a hundred percent and stays on what you were looking at.
Click the percentage once. The stop menu opens as it always did.
Pick 400% from that menu, then double click the number again.
Switch to the wand, the text tool and the crop tool in turn and watch the row stay level.
Drag the window narrow until the slider and the grid chip step out.

evaluate: Does the row read as one strip now, or does something still sit high or low?
Is 48pt the right height for the whole row, or should the row be slimmer than the tool bar was?
After a single click, does the stop menu open fast enough? It waits up to a quarter of a second to see whether a second click is coming.
Is double clicking the number the gesture you reach for, or would you rather it landed somewhere else?
When you go back to actual size, does the picture stay where you expected it to?
rough: The single click now waits before opening the menu: up to a quarter of a second, or your own double click interval if you have set a faster one. It cannot be avoided while both gestures live on the same number, because a menu takes every event the moment it opens, so the second click of a double click would land inside it. If the wait ever reads as lag, say so and the double click can move somewhere else.

Going back to actual size is not on the undo stack. Zoom never has been in Photonz: undo is for edits to the picture, and undoing a zoom would put back a view you did not ask to keep. The double click leaves the document and its history untouched, which the walk checks.

The heights were measured, not eyeballed. Before: tools 48pt, colours 45pt, zoom 35pt, all on centre line 800. After, in every state a walk could reach (wide, narrow, grid on, shape tool, wand, text, crop, adjusting the grid): 48pt each, one centre line. One number in EditorChromeLayout decides it now, so a new group cannot drift.
Screen Recording was granted, so the pictures here are real captures of the window rather than offscreen renders.
